chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Aamir, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Mahziyar, from Quteiba Al-A'sha, who said:

I went to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) to visit a son of his, and I found him at the door; he was worried and sad. So I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, how is the child?' He said, 'By Allah, he is still with it.' Then he entered and stayed for a while, then came out to us, and his face had turned pale, and the change and sadness had gone.

He said, 'I hoped that the child had recovered, so I said, 'How is the child, may I be sacrificed for you?' He said, 'And he has gone to his Way.' So I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, you were worried and sad while he was alive, and I saw your state at this time, and he has died in a state other than that. So how is this?'
So he said, 'We, the People of the Household, only panic before the calamity. So when the Command of Allah occurs, we are pleased with its decree and submit to its command.'

key_terms.أَهْلَ الْبَيْتِ: The People of the Household (Ahl al-Bayt)
key_terms.يَجْزَعُ: To panic or show intense anxiety/grief

ai.seo_question: Why did the Imam appear sad before his son died and calm after?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the psychological and spiritual state of the Ahl al-Bayt, distinguishing between pre-emptive anxiety (jaz') regarding potential loss and post-event contentment (rida) with the divine decree. It serves as a practical model for believers, illustrating that deep love for loved ones manifests as sorrow before their passing, while acceptance follows the actualization of God's will. This narrative reinforces the concept of 'sabr jamil' (beautiful patience) by showing that emotional distress does not contradict spiritual submission.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Abdullah Bin Aamir, from Ali Bin Mahziyar, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Bin Mahziyar, from Quteyba Al A’asha who said,

‘I went over to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> to comfort him<sup>asws</sup> for a son of his<sup>asws</sup> (who was sick), and I found him<sup>asws</sup> at the door, and he<sup>asws</sup> was worried, in grief. So I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! How is the child?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! He is still with it’. Then he<sup>asws</sup> entered (the house) and remained for a while, then came out to us, and his face had turned pale, the change and the grief had gone.

He (the narrator) said, ‘I hoped he had become better, so I said, ‘How is the child, may I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And he has gone to His<sup>azwj</sup> Way’. So I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! When he was alive you<sup>asws</sup> were worried, in grief, and I see your<sup>asws</sup> state at this time and he has died, and it is other than that state. So how is this?’

So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘We<sup>asws</sup>, the People<sup>asws</sup> of the Household, we<sup>asws</sup> panic before the difficulty (bereavement). So when the Command of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> occurs, we<sup>asws</sup> are pleased with it and submit to His<sup>azwj</sup> Command’.
en.sarwar: 11. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Amir from Ali ibn Mahziyar from al-Hassan ibn Muhammad ibn Mahziyar from al-Qutaybah al-A’sha’ who has said the following:

“Once I visited abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, to also visit his son who was ill. I met him at the door and he was sorrowful and depressed. I asked, ‘May Allah keep my soul in service of your cause, how is your child?’ He replied, ‘By Allah, he is about to die.’ He then went inside the house and after a while came back to us, he looked bright and without any sign of depression.

I had a longing that this can be a sign of the recovery of the child and I asked, ‘May Allah keep my soul in service of your cause, how is the child?’ He replied, ‘He just passed away.’ I then asked, ‘May Allah keep my soul in service of your cause, I found you, when the child was still alive, so much depressed and sad but now, when the child is dead, I see you have changed so much with brightness. How is all this happened?’
He replied, ‘We, the family of the Holy Prophet, cry (to Allah) for help before the fall of misfortune but once the command of Allah is issued, we accept it and submit ourselves to His command.’”
